Name: Canberra
NameDerivation: A locality name derived from an Aboriginal word which is held to mean 'meeting place'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Canberra covers an area in central ACT consisting of the Districts of Canberra Central, Kowen, Majura, part of Belconnen, part of Jerrabomberra, part of Molonglo Valley, part of Weston Creek and part of Woden Valley.
ProductsIndustries: Mainly residential with tourism, retail and some light industry at Fyshwick and Beard

Name: Fenner
NameDerivation: Named after Professor Frank Fenner AC CMG MBE FAA FRS FRACP FRCP, 1914-2010, eminent scientist of national and international renown who made significant contributions to improving the wellbeing of humanity.
LocationDescription: The Division of Fenner covers an area in the north of the ACT consisting of the Districts of Gungahlin, Hall and part of Belconnen. The Division of Fenner also includes the Jervis Bay Territory.
ProductsIndustries: Mainly residential with tourism, retail and some light industry at Mitchell

Name: Banks
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Joseph Banks, 1743-1820. Banks was a botanist who accompanied Captain Cook on his voyage to Australia in 1770 and recorded his impressions of the Australian east coast, noting plants, insects, molluscs, reptiles, birds, fish, quadrupeds etc., as well as Aboriginal customs.
LocationDescription: The Division of Banks consists of part of the Canterbury Bankstown Council and part of the Georges River Council.

Name: Barton
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir Edmund Barton GCMG KC, 1849-1920. Barton was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia, the first Prime Minister of Australia (1901-03) and a Justice of the High Court (1903-20).
LocationDescription: The Division of Barton consists of part of the Bayside Council, part of the Canterbury Bankstown Council and part of the Georges River Council.

Name: Bennelong
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Bennelong, 1764?-1813. Bennelong was a young Aboriginal man who was captured by Governor Arthur Phillip in 1789. He was later taken to England where he met the King.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bennelong consists of the Council of the Municipality of Hunters Hill, Lane Cove Municipal Council, the Council of the City of Ryde, part of the Council of the City of Parramatta and part of the Willoughby City Council.

Name: Berowra
NameDerivation: Named after the area in which the electoral division is located. The name 'Berowra' is believed to be an Aborginal word for 'place of many winds'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Berowra consists of the Council of the Shire of Hornsby, part of the Council of the City of Parramatta, part of the Ku-ring-gai Council and part of The Hills Shire Council.

Name: Blaxland
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Gregory Blaxland, 1778-1853. Blaxland was an early Australian explorer who was a member of the first European party to successfully cross the Blue Mountains in New South Wales.
LocationDescription: The Division of Blaxland consists of part of the Canterbury Bankstown Council, part of the Cumberland Council, part of the Fairfield City Council, part of the Council of the City of Parramatta and part of the Strathfield Municipal Council.

Name: Bradfield
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dr John Job Crew Bradfield CMG, 1867-1943. Bradfield was a civil engineer who was associated with the Cataract and Burrinjuck Dams and was instrumental in the design of the Sydney Harbour Bridge.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bradfield consists of part of the Ku-ring-gai Council, part of the North Sydney Council and part of the Willoughby City Council.

Name: Calare
NameDerivation: Named after the Aboriginal name for the Lachlan River.
LocationDescription: The Division of Calare consists of Bathurst Regional Council, Blayney Shire Council, Cabonne Council, City of Lithgow Council, Mid-Western Regional Council, Oberon Council, Orange City Council and part of the Dubbo Regional Council.

Name: Chifley
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Joseph Benedict Chifley, 1885-1951. Chifley was Prime Minister of Australia (1945-49) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1928-31 and 1940-51).
LocationDescription: The Division of Chifley consists of part of the Blacktown City Council.

Name: Cook
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir Joseph Cook GCMG PC, 1860-1947, Prime Minister of Australia (1913-14); and Captain James Cook FRS, 1728-79, a navigator in the Royal Navy credited as the first European to discover the east coast of Australia in 1770.
LocationDescription: The Division of Cook consists of part of the Bayside Council, part of the Georges River Council and part of the Sutherland Shire Council.

Name: Cowper
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Charles Cowper CMG KCMG, 1807-75. Cowper was a statesman who served as Premier of New South Wales on five occasions.
LocationDescription: The Division of Cowper consists of Bellingen Shire Council, Kempsey Shire Council, Nambucca Valley Council, part of the Coffs Harbour City Council and part of the Port Macquarie-Hastings Council.

Name: Cunningham
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Allan Cunningham, 1791-1839. Cunningham was a botanist who accompanied many explorations along Australia's east coast and is credited with discovering Pandora's Pass, the Darling Downs and Cunningham's Gap.
LocationDescription: The Division of Cunningham consists of part of the Wollondilly Shire Council and part of the Wollongong City Council.

Name: Dobell
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir William Dobell OBE, 1899-1970. Dobell was a prominent Australian painter and portrait artist who won the Archibald Prize in 1943.
LocationDescription: The Division of Dobell consists of part of the Central Coast Council.

Name: Eden-Monaro
NameDerivation: Named after the two areas in which the electoral division is located. The name 'Monaro' is variously believed to be derived from the Aboriginal word 'Maneroo', meaning plain, or an Aboriginal word meaning 'the navel' or 'a woman's breasts'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Eden-Monaro consists of Bega Valley Shire Council, Goulburn Mulwaree Council, Queanbeyan-Palerang Regional Council, Snowy Monaro Regional Council and part of the Eurobodalla Shire Council.

Name: Farrer
NameDerivation: Named in honour of William James Farrer, 1845-1906. Farrer was a noted wheat breeder and experimentalist.
LocationDescription: The Division of Farrer consists of Albury City Council, Balranald Shire Council, Berrigan Shire Council, Carrathool Shire Council, Edward River Council, Federation Council, Greater Hume Shire Council, Griffith City Council, Hay Shire Council, Leeton Shire Council, Murray River Council, Murrumbidgee Council, Narrandera Shire Council and Wentworth Shire Council.

Name: Fowler
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Elizabeth Lilian Maud Fowler MBE, 1887-1954. Fowler was the first woman mayor in Australia (1938-39). The division was so named to also honour the contribution of women to local government.
LocationDescription: The Division of Fowler consists of part of the Cumberland Council, part of the Fairfield City Council and part of the Liverpool City Council.

Name: Gilmore
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dame Mary Jean Gilmore DBE, 1865-1962. Gilmore was a noted poet and prose writer.
LocationDescription: The Division of Gilmore consists of the Council of the Municipality of Kiama, Shoalhaven City Council and part of the Eurobodalla Shire Council.

Name: Grayndler
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Edward Grayndler OBE, 1867-1943. Grayndler was a foundation member of the Amalgamated Shearers' Union of Australasia in 1886 and in 1895 was appointed shearer's union organiser for the Australian Workers' Union. He was a member of the Industrial Delegation to the USA in 1927.
LocationDescription: The Division of Grayndler consists of part of the Burwood Council, part of the Canterbury Bankstown Council, part of the Inner West Council and part of the Council of the City of Sydney.

Name: Greenway
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Francis Greenway, 1777-1837. Greenway, a former convict, was a noted colonial architect.
LocationDescription: The Division of Greenway consists of part of the Blacktown City Council and part of The Hills Shire Council.

Name: Hughes
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. William Morris Hughes CH KC, 1862-1952. Hughes was Prime Minister of Australia (1915-23) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-52).
LocationDescription: The Division of Hughes consists of part of the Campbelltown City Council, part of the Liverpool City Council and part of the Sutherland Shire Council.

Name: Hume
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Hamilton Hume, 1797-1873. Hume was an explorer of south-eastern Australia. He was part of the first expedition to travel overland from Sydney to Port Phillip and part of the first European expedition to discover the Darling River.
LocationDescription: The Division of Hume consists of part of the Camden Council, part of the Liverpool City Council, part of the Penrith City Council and part of the Wollondilly Shire Council.

Name: Hunter
NameDerivation: Named for the Hunter River, which was part of the electoral division when it was first created. The river was discovered by John Shortland in 1797 and named after Captain John Hunter RN, the second Governor of the Colony of New South Wales (1795-1800).
LocationDescription: The Division of Hunter consists of Singleton Council, part of the Cessnock City Council, part of the Lake Macquarie City Council and part of the Maitland City Council.

Name: Kingsford Smith
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Charles Edward Kingsford Smith MC AFC, 1897-1935. Kingsford Smith was Australia's most famous aviator. He made the first flight from the United States to Australia in 1928, as well as many other notable flights including the first non-stop crossing of mainland Australia.
LocationDescription: The Division of Kingsford Smith consists of part of the Bayside Council, part of the Inner West Council, part of the Randwick City Council and part of the Council of the City of Sydney.

Name: Lindsay
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Norman Alfred Lindsay, 1879-1969. Lindsay was a prominent Australian painter, novelist and artist who is known for creating 'The Magic Pudding'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Lindsay consists of part of the Penrith City Council.

Name: Lyne
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir William John Lyne, 1844-1913. Lyne was a participant in the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia and was the first member of the Australian Parliament to be offered a commission to form a government.
LocationDescription: The Division of Lyne consists of Dungog Shire Council, Mid-Coast Council, part of the Maitland City Council, part of the Port Macquarie-Hastings Council and part of the Port Stephens Council.

Name: Macarthur
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of Elizabeth Macarthur, 1766-1850, and Captain John Macarthur, 1767-1834. The Macarthurs were early settlers in New South Wales and founders of the Australian merino wool industry.
LocationDescription: The Division of Macarthur consists of part of the Camden Council, part of the Campbelltown City Council and part of the Liverpool City Council.

Name: Mackellar
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Isobel Marion Dorothea Mackellar OBE, 1885-1968. Mackellar was a poet and author who was best known for writing 'My Country'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Mackellar consists of part of the Northern Beaches Council.

Name: Macquarie
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Major-General Lachlan Macquarie, 1761-1824. Macquarie was Governor of the Colony of New South Wales (1810-21). The area covered by the electoral division when it was first established in 1901 was also known as the Macquarie district.
LocationDescription: The Division of Macquarie consists of Blue Mountains City Council, Hawkesbury City Council, part of the Penrith City Council and part of the Wollondilly Shire Council.

Name: Mitchell
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Thomas Livingstone Mitchell, 1792-1855. Mitchell was a noted surveyor, who built and improved many roads in New South Wales, and an explorer who conducted several expeditions in south-eastern Australia, including following the courses of the Darling, Lachlan and Murray Rivers.
LocationDescription: The Division of Mitchell consists of part of the Council of the City of Parramatta and part of The Hills Shire Council.

Name: New England
NameDerivation: Named after the area covered by the electoral division. It is believed the area has been known by this name due to the similarity of its climate, fruits and cultivation to England.
LocationDescription: The Division of New England consists of Armidale Regional Council, Glen Innes Severn Council, Gwydir Shire Council, Inverell Shire Council, Liverpool Plains Shire Council, Muswellbrook Shire Council, Tamworth Regional Council, Tenterfield Shire Council, Upper Hunter Shire Council, Uralla Shire Council and Walcha Council.

Name: Newcastle
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division. Newcastle was named by Governor King in 1804.
LocationDescription: The Division of Newcastle consists of part of the Lake Macquarie City Council and part of the Newcastle City Council.

Name: Page
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir Earle Christmas Grafton Page GCMG CH, 1880-1961. Page was caretaker Prime Minister of Australia (7 April-16 April 1939) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1919-61).
LocationDescription: The Division of Page consists of Clarence Valley Council, Kyogle Council, Lismore City Council, Richmond Valley Council, part of the Ballina Shire Council and part of the Coffs Harbour City Council.

Name: Parkes
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Henry Parkes KCMG GCMG, 1815-96. Parkes was a statesman who advocated for electoral and constitutional reform in the colony and land reform. As a result of his early promotion of federation of the colonies, Parkes is known as the 'Father of Federation'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Parkes consists of Bland Shire Council, Bogan Shire Council, Bourke Shire Council, Brewarrina Shire Council, Broken Hill City Council, Central Darling Shire Council, Forbes Shire Council, Gilgandra Shire Council, Lachlan Shire Council, Moree Plains Shire Council, Narrabri Shire Council, Narromine Shire Council, Parkes Shire Council, Walgett Shire Council, Warren Shire Council, Warrumbungle Shire Council, Unincorporated Far West Region NSW, and part of the Dubbo Regional Council.

Name: Parramatta
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division. 'Parramatta' is variously believed to be the Dharuk word for 'head of the river', or derived from an Aboriginal word meaning 'place where the eels lie down' or 'dark jungle head of a river', or from the name of the tribe 'Burramattagal'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Parramatta consists of part of the Blacktown City Council, part of the Cumberland Council and part of the Council of the City of Parramatta.

Name: Reid
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir George Houstoun Reid KC GCB GCMG, 1845-1918. Reid was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia, Prime Minister of Australia (1904-05) and Australia's first High Commissioner to London.
LocationDescription: The Division of Reid consists of the City of Canada Bay Council, part of the Burwood Council, part of the Cumberland Council, part of the Inner West Council, part of the Council of the City of Parramatta and part of the Strathfield Municipal Council.

Name: Richmond
NameDerivation: Named after the area covered by the electoral division.
LocationDescription: The Division of Richmond consists of Byron Shire Council, Tweed Shire Council and part of the Ballina Shire Council.

Name: Robertson
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir John Robertson KCMG, 1816-91. Robertson was a statesman who advocated for electoral and constitutional reform in the colony and land reform.
LocationDescription: The Division of Robertson consists of part of the Central Coast Council.

Name: Shortland
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Naval Lieutenant John Shortland, 1769-1810. Shortland named the Hunter River, made the first chart of the harbour and collected samples of coal near what would become Shortland.
LocationDescription: The Division of Shortland consists of part of the Central Coast Council, part of the Lake Macquarie City Council and part of the Newcastle City Council.

Name: Sydney
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division. The name 'Sydney' was used by Captain Arthur Phillip in honour of Thomas Townshend, First Viscount Sydney, who as British Home Secretary submitted the plan for a convict settlement at Botany Bay.
LocationDescription: The Division of Sydney consists of part of the Inner West Council, part of the Council of the City of Sydney, and Lord Howe Island.

Name: Whitlam
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Hon. Edward Gough Whitlam AC QC, 1916-2014. Whitlam was Prime Minister of Australia (1972-75) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1952-78).
LocationDescription: The Division of Whitlam consists of Shellharbour City Council, Wingecarribee Shire Council and part of the Wollongong City Council.

Name: Warringah
NameDerivation: Named after the area in which the electoral division is located. 'Warringah' is believed to be an Aboriginal word meaning 'sign of rain', 'across the waves' or 'sea'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Warringah consists of Mosman Municipal Council, part of the North Sydney Council and part of the Northern Beaches Council.

Name: Wentworth
NameDerivation: Named in honour of William Charles Wentworth, 1790 -1872. Wentworth accompanied Blaxland and Lawson on their 1813 crossing of the Blue Mountains and advocated the establishment of free and representative government.
LocationDescription: The Division of Wentworth consists of Waverley Council, Woollahra Municipal Council, part of the Randwick City Council and part of the Council of the City of Sydney.

Name: Werriwa
NameDerivation: 'Werriwa' was the Aboriginal name for Lake George, which was located in the electoral division when it was first established in 1901. The name 'Werriwa' is believed to be an Aboriginal word meaning 'deep water' or 'sick crawfish'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Werriwa consists of part of the Campbelltown City Council, part of the Fairfield City Council and part of the Liverpool City Council.

Name: Bowman
NameDerivation: Named in honour of David Bowman, 1860-1916, one of the first members of the Labour party in the Queensland Parliament (1899-1902 and 1904-1916) who rendered valuable service in the interests of the community.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bowman consists of part of the Redland City Council and part of the Brisbane City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Farming, retail and industrial activities. Tourism on the Islands and a Winery at Mount Cotton.

Name: Brisbane
NameDerivation: Named in recognition of the City of Brisbane.
LocationDescription: The Division of Brisbane consists of part of the Brisbane City Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mostly residential but contains some light industry. It includes the Queensland Parliament House and Brisbane City Council Chambers. Many Commonwealth Government, State Government and business administrative offices are found in the area.

Name: Capricornia
NameDerivation: Named in recognition of the Tropic of Capricorn.
LocationDescription: The Division of Capricornia consists of Isaac Regional Council, Livingstone Shire Council, part of the Mackay Regional Council, part of the Rockhampton Regional Council and part of the Whitsunday Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Primary production, grains, beef cattle, grazing, fishing, coal mining, meat works, dairy products and tourism.

Name: Dawson
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Andrew Dawson, 1863-1910, Premier of Queensland (1899-1903).
LocationDescription: The Division of Dawson consists of part of the Burdekin Shire Council, part of the Mackay Regional Council, part of the Townsville City Council and part of the Whitsunday Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Various small crops, prawn and fish farms, sugar growing and refining, beef cattle, coal mining related industries, abattoirs and tourism.

Name: Fadden
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Arthur William Fadden, 1895-1973, Prime Minister of Australia (August-October 1941) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1936-58).
LocationDescription: The Division of Fadden consists of part of the Gold Coast City Council and part of the Redland City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Residential areas are concentrated in the south with semi-rural in the north. Commercial activities include tourism, market gardens, sugar cane farming, and light industry including boat building.

Name: Fairfax
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Ruth Beatrice Fairfax OBE, 1878-1948, a founder of the Country Women's Association and its first Queensland president.
LocationDescription: The Division of Fairfax consists of part of the Sunshine Coast Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Avocados, ginger, sugar cane, fruit juice, tropical and exotic fruits, dairy and beef cattle, tourism, health care, construction and infrastructure industries.

Name: Fisher
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Andrew Fisher, 1862-1928, Prime Minister of Australia (1908-09, 1910-13, 1914-15) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-15).
LocationDescription: The Division of Fisher consists of part of the Sunshine Coast Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Health care, retail, tourism, education and construction and development are the major employers. Other industries include pineapple, orchard and flower crops, dairy and beef cattle farming, and horse racing.

Name: Forde
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Francis Michael Forde, 1890-1983, Prime Minister of Australia (July 1945) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1922-46).
LocationDescription: The Division of Forde consists of part of the Gold Coast City Council and part of the Logan City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Retail, commercial and industrial activities.

Name: Griffith
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Samuel Walker Griffith QC, 1845-1920, for his involvement with Federation and the development of the Australian Constitution and who was the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Australia (1903-19).
LocationDescription: The Division of Griffith consists of part of the Brisbane City Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mostly residential with some food processing and light industry. It is also the location of the world famous Brisbane Cricket Ground known as The Gabba.

Name: Groom
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Littleton Ernest Groom, 1867-1936, Speaker of the House of Representatives (1926-29) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-29 and 1931-36).
LocationDescription: The Division of Groom consists of part of the Toowoomba Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: This area is noted for its rich and diverse range of products and industries including agriculture, retailing and food processing as well as for the provision of educational and community services. Toowoomba is known as the Garden City. The University of Southern Queensland is located in Toowoomba while the Army Aviation Centre is based at Oakey.

Name: Herbert
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Robert George Wyndham Herbert, 1831-1905, the first Premier of Queensland (1859-66).
LocationDescription: The Division of Herbert consists of Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council, part of Hinchinbrook Shire Council and part of the Townsville City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Copper, nickel and zinc refineries, bulk sugar terminal, and tropical fruits, prawn and fishing industry, beef cattle and tourism. Townsville, noted for its port facilities, is also home to James Cook University, the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority and large defence establishments at Lavarack Barracks (Army) and Garbutt (RAAF).

Name: Hinkler
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Herbert John (Bert) Hinkler DSM AFC, 1892-1933, aviator who was the first person to fly solo from England to Australia in 1928.
LocationDescription: The Division of Hinkler consists of part of the Bundaberg Regional Council and part of the Fraser Coast Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Sugar, a myriad of small crops including tomatoes, avocados and macadamia nuts, rum, fishing, seafood industries and tourism.

Name: Kennedy
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Edmund Besley Kennedy, 1818-48, surveyor and explorer who sought to find an overland route to the Gulf of Carpentaria.
LocationDescription: The Division of Kennedy consists of Boulia Shire Council, Burke Shire Council, Cassowary Coast Regional Council, Charters Towers Regional Shire Council, Cloncurry Shire Council, Croydon Shire Council, Doomadgee Aboriginal Shire Council, Etheridge Shire Council, Flinders Shire Council, McKinlay Shire Council, Mornington Shire Council, Mt Isa City Council, Richmond Shire Council, Tablelands Regional Council, Yarrabah Aboriginal Shire Council, part of the Burdekin Shire Council, part of the Cairns Regional Council, part of the Carpentaria Shire Council, part of the Hinchinbrook Shire Council, part of the Mareeba Shire Council and part of the Townsville City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Mainly primary production including grains (sorghum, sunflowers, wheat), beef cattle, cotton, coal mining, gemstones, sheep, sugar, agricultural services, copper, gold, silver, tin, lead, zinc, uranium, fishing (prawns, crabs, barramundi), marble, tobacco, fruit and vegetables, peanuts, dairy products and tourism.

Name: Leichhardt
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Friedrich Wilhelm Ludwig Leichhardt, 1813-48, naturalist and explorer of the area from Moreton Bay to Port Essington.
LocationDescription: The Division of Leichhardt consists of Aurukun Shire Council, Cook Shire Council, Douglas Shire Council, Hope Vale Aboriginal Shire Council, Kowanyama Aboriginal Shire Council, Lockhart River Aboriginal Shire Council, Mapoon Aboriginal Shire Council, Napranum Aboriginal Shire Council, Northern Peninsula Area Regional Council, Pormpuraaw Aboriginal Shire Council, Torres Shire Council, Torres Strait Island Regional Council, Weipa Town Council, Wujal Wujal Aboriginal Shire Council, part of the Cairns Regional Council, part of the Carpentaria Shire Council and part of the Mareeba Shire Council.
ProductsIndustries: Sugar, tropical fruit, aquaculture, cattle, fishing, mining and tourism.

Name: Lilley
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Charles Lilley, 1827-97, Premier of Queensland (1868-70), member of the Queensland Parliament (1860-74) and responsible for introducing free education into Queensland.
LocationDescription: The Division of Lilley consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Moreton Bay Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mostly residential but includes Brisbane's domestic and international airports, light and heavy engineering, sea-cargo facilities, chemical production, warehousing (civilian and military), oil refining and storage and various small industries.

Name: Maranoa
NameDerivation: Named for the district which is watered by the Maranoa River.  The name 'Maranoa' is possibly a corruption of the Mandandanji words 'mara' for duck and 'ngoa' for egg.
LocationDescription: The Division of Maranoa consists of Balonne Shire Council, Barcaldine Regional Council, Barcoo Shire Council, Blackall Tambo Regional Council, Bulloo Shire Council, Diamantina Shire Council, Goondiwindi Regional Council, Longreach Regional Council, Maranoa Regional Council, Murweh Shire Council, Paroo Shire Council, Quilpie Shire Council, Western Downs Regional Council, Winton Shire Council, part of the South Burnett Regional Council, part of the Southern Downs Regional Council and part of the Toowoomba Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Mainly primary production including coal, oil, gas, orchards, cotton, grain, cattle and sheep.

Name: McPherson
NameDerivation: Named after the McPherson Range for the range which runs north-west from Mount Glennie.
LocationDescription: The Division of McPherson consists of part of the Gold Coast City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Tourism and associated industries and a variety of small industries.

Name: Moncrieff
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Gladys Lillian Moncrieff, 1892-1976, light opera and musical comedy singer.
LocationDescription: The Division of Moncrieff consists of part of the Gold Coast City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Tourism and associated industries and a variety of small industries.

Name: Moreton
NameDerivation: Named after Morton Bay, the bay bounded by Cape Moreton and Point Lookout,.  The bay was marked on his chart of May 1770 by Lieutenant James Cook RN, navigator on HM Bark Endeavour.
LocationDescription: The Division of Moreton consists of part of the Brisbane City Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mainly residential with some light industrial and commercial activities. A light aircraft airport is in Archerfield.

Name: Oxley
NameDerivation: Named in honour of John Joseph Oxley, 1784-1828, considered to be one of the greatest explorers and early pioneers of Southern Queensland.
LocationDescription: The Division of Oxley consists of part of the Brisbane City Council, part of the Ipswich City Council and part of the Logan City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Railway workshops, industrial, light industrial and commercial activities.

Name: Petrie
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Andrew Petrie, 1798-1872, a noted civil engineer, pioneer, explorer and the first free settler in Brisbane in 1837.
LocationDescription: The Division of Petrie consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Moreton Bay Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mainly residential with some light industrial and commercial activities.

Name: Rankin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dame Annabelle Jane Mary Rankin DBE, 1908-86, first Queensland woman elected to the Senate (1947-71) and the first Australian woman to hold a top-level diplomatic post as High Commissioner to New Zealand (1971-74).
LocationDescription: The Division of Rankin consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Logan City Council.
ProductsIndustries: A diversity of land use, from residential and acreage suburbs to light industrial.

Name: Ryan
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Thomas Joseph Ryan, 1876-1921, Premier of Queensland (1915-19) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1919-21).
LocationDescription: The Division of Ryan consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Moreton Bay Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: The area is mainly residential and acreage suburbs with some commercial and retail activities. The University of Queensland is located on the Brisbane River at St Lucia, while all of Brisbane's television transmitters are on Mount Coot-tha. By way of contrast, some farming still occurs in the outlying suburbs and the division also includes a large portion of Brisbane Forest Park.

Name: Wide Bay
NameDerivation: Named after the bay sighted by Lieutenant James Cook RN, navigator on HM Bark Endeavour, on 18 May 1770.
LocationDescription: The Division of Wide Bay consists of Cherbourg Aboriginal Shire Council, Gympie Regional Council, Noosa Shire Council, part of the Fraser Coast Regional Council, part of the South Burnett Regional Council and part of the Sunshine Coast Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Eco-tourism (Fraser Island), historical attractions (Maryborough), natural attractions (Cooloola Coast) timber, dairying, grain, grazing, sugar, tropical fruit orchards, and railway rolling stock (including Queensland's 'tilt' trains).

Name: Adelaide
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division.  The city was named by King William IV after his Consort, Queen Adelaide.
LocationDescription: The Division of Adelaide consists of Adelaide City Council, City of Prospect, Corporation of the Town of Walkerville, part of the City of Burnside, part of the City of Charles Sturt, part of the City of Port Adelaide Enfield, part of the City of Unley and part of the City of West Torrens.
ProductsIndustries: Adelaide central business district, Adelaide oval, brewery, hospitals, light industry, markets, military barracks, South Australia Parliament and Government House and universities.

Name: Barker
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Captain Collet Barker, 1784-1831.  Barker explored the eastern shore of Gulf St Vincent, Mount Lofty and the mouth of the Murray River.
LocationDescription: The Division of Barker consists of Berri Barmera Council, City of Mount Gambier, Coorong District Council, District Council of Grant, District Council of Karoonda East Murray, District Council of Loxton Waikerie, District Council of Robe, Kingston District Council, Naracoorte Lucindale Council, Mid Murray Council, Renmark Paringa Council, Rural City of Murray Bridge, Southern Mallee District Council, Tatiara District Council, Wattle Range Council, part of the Barossa Council, part of the Light Regional Council,  part of the Outback Community Authority and unincorporated Riverland.
ProductsIndustries: Beef and dairy cattle, cropping, fishing, forestry, fresh and dried fruit, motor sports, paper products, sheep, timber, transport, tourism, vegetables and viticulture.

Name: Boothby
NameDerivation: Named in honour of William Robinson Boothby CMG, 1829-1903.  Boothby introduced many electoral innovations in South Australia and from 1856 to 1903 superintended every State parliamentary election and drafted every Electoral Act in South Australia.
LocationDescription: The Division of Boothby consists of City of Holdfast Bay, part of the City of Marion, part of the City of Mitcham and part of the City of Unley.
ProductsIndustries: Major retailing, army camp and military barracks, tertiary education, tourism, several hospitals and various small industries.

Name: Grey
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir George Grey, 1812-98.  Grey explored parts of north-western Australia and was Governor of South Australia (1841-45).
LocationDescription: The Division of Grey consists of Adelaide Plains Council, Anangu Pitjantjatjara Yankunytjatjara, City of Port Lincoln, Clare and Gilbert Valleys Council, Corporation of the City of Whyalla, District Council of Barunga West, District Council of Ceduna, District Council of Cleve, District Council of Coober Pedy, District Council of Elliston, District Council of Franklin Harbour, District Council of Kimba, District Council of Lower Eyre Peninsula, District Council of Mount Remarkable, District Council of Orroroo Carrieton, District Council of  Peterborough, District Council of Streaky Bay, District Council of the Copper Coast, District Council of Tumby Bay, Flinders Ranges Council, Maralinga Tjarutja, Municipal Council of Roxby Downs, Northern Areas Council, Port Augusta City Council, Port Pirie Regional Council, Regional Council of Goyder, Wakefield Regional Council, Wudinna District Council, Yorke Peninsula Council, part of Light Regional Council, Pastoral Unincorporated Area and unincorporated area Whyalla.
ProductsIndustries: Aquaculture, cattle, copper, fishing, gas, gypsum, iron ore, lead smelting, oil, opals, steel industry, salt, slate, tourism, uranium, viticulture, wheat and wool.

Name: Hindmarsh
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir John Hindmarsh KH RN, 1785-1860. Hindmarsh was the first Governor of the Colony of South Australia (1836-38).
LocationDescription: The Division of Hindmarsh consists of part of the City of Charles Sturt, part of the City of Port Adelaide Enfield and part of the City of West Torrens.
ProductsIndustries: Aviation, cement, commercial fishing, electricity generation, flour mills, grain bulk handling, heavy engineering, major retailing, manufacturing industry, motion picture production, numerous sporting venues, petroleum storage, police academy, shipping, small industries, stevedoring, tourism, warship & submarine construction, waste disposal and wool stores.

Name: Kingston
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Charles Cameron Kingston, 1850-1908.  Kingston was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-08).
LocationDescription: The Division of Kingston consists of part of the City of Marion and part of the City of Onkaparinga.
ProductsIndustries: Construction, clothing, desalination plant, engineering, major retailing, optical lenses and various light industries.

Name: Makin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Hon. Norman John Oswald Makin AO, 1889-1982.  Makin was a Member of the House of Representatives (1919-46 and 1954-63) and Speaker of the House of Representatives (1929-31).
LocationDescription: The Division of Makin consists of part of the City of Port Adelaide Enfield, part of the City of Salisbury and part of the City of Tea Tree Gully.
ProductsIndustries: Aviation, brick making, commercial and retail industry, higher education, hobby farmers, horse studs, light manufacturing, Modbury Hospital, tourism and wineries.

Name: Mayo
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dr Helen Mary Mayo OBE, 1878-1967. Mayo worked in the areas of maternal and child health and welfare in South Australia, was the first woman elected to an Australian University Council  in 1914 and co-founded of the Mothers' and Babies' Health Association in 1927.
LocationDescription: The Division of Mayo consists of Alexandrina Council, City of Victor Harbor, District Council of Yankalilla, Kangaroo Island Council, Mount Barker District Council,  part of the Adelaide Hills Council, part of the City of Mitcham and part of the City of Onkaparinga.
ProductsIndustries: Apples, Army barracks at Woodside, beef, breweries, cereals, cherries, copper mines, dairying, forestry, natural spring water, pears, sheep, smallgoods, tourism and wine.

Name: Sturt
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Captain Charles Sturt 1795-1869.  Sturt conducted several journeys of exploration into Australia's interior, served for a period as commandant of the garrison on Norfolk Island and served in the South Australian public service.
LocationDescription: The Division of Sturt consists of Campbelltown City Council, City of Norwood Payneham and St Peters, part of Adelaide Hills Council, part of the City of Burnside, part of the City of Port Adelaide Enfield, part of the City of Tea Tree Gully and part of the City of Unley.
ProductsIndustries: Commercial and retail, light industry, University of South Australia campus and viticulture.

Name: Bass
NameDerivation: Named in honour of George Bass, 1771-1803.  Bass was a surgeon, scientist and explorer who was one of those responsible for the early geographical investigation of the Australian coast.  Bass' explorations included the islands in Bass Strait, Tamar estuary, Derwent estuary and Mount Wellington.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bass is located on Launceston and consists of the City of Launceston, Municipality of Dorset, Municipality of Flinders Island, Municipality of George Town, Municipality of West Tamar. The Division of Bass includes Flinders Island.
ProductsIndustries: Aluminium and ferrous metal smelting, brewery, cattle (dairy and beef) farming, manufacturing, mining, ports and shipping, ship building, timber, tourism, fishing, wineries and wool.

Name: Braddon
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Edward Nicholas Coventry Braddon KCMG, 1829-1904, who was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-04).
LocationDescription: The Division of Braddon is focused on Burnie and Devonport and also consists of the City of Burnie, Municipality of Central Coast, Municipality of Circular Head, City of Devonport, Municipality of King Island, Municipality of Latrobe, Municipality of Waratah-Wynard and Municipality of West Coast. The Division of Braddon includes King Island.
ProductsIndustries: Forestry, fishing, aquaculture, kelp harvesting, dairying, beef cattle production, and vegetable, poppy and pyrethrum growing are major primary industries. Vegetable processing, cheese manufacture, sawmilling and woodchipping complement these activities. Mining and tourism are major industries in Braddon.

Name: Franklin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir John Franklin KCH RN, 1786-1847, Lieutenant-Governor of Van Diemen's Land (1837-43), in recognition of his service to the colony.
LocationDescription: The Division of Franklin consists of the Municipality of Huon Valley, part of the City of Clarence and part of the Municipality of Kingborough. The Division of Franklin includes Macquarie Island.
ProductsIndustries: Apples, pears, small fruits, aquaculture, fishing, beef cattle, sheep, forestry, cottage industry, vineyards and tourism.

Name: Lyons
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of Joseph Aloysius Lyons CH, 1879-1939, Prime Minister of Australia (1932-39) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1929-39), and Dame Enid Muriel Lyons, DGBE(C) AD, 1897-1981, first woman member of the House of Representatives (1943-51).
LocationDescription: The Division of Lyons consists of the Municipality of Break O'Day, Municipality of Brighton, Municipality of Central Highlands, Municipality of Derwent Valley, Municipality of Dorset, Municipality of Flinders, Municipality of Glamorgan-Spring Bay, Municipality of Kentish, Municipality of Meander Valley, Municipality of Northern Midlands, Municipality of Sorell, Municipality of Southern Midlands, Municipality of Tasman and part of the City of Clarence.
ProductsIndustries: Fishing, forestry, wool, cattle (dairy and beef), fruit, wine, hydro-power generation, mining and tourism.

Name: Paterson
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of Colonel William Paterson, 1755-1810, a soldier and botanist who served as Lieutenant-Governor of the Colony of New South Wales (1794-95, 1800-08 and 1809); and Andrew Barton 'Banjo' Paterson CBE, 1864-1941, a journalist, war correspondent and poet.
LocationDescription: The Division of Paterson consists of part of the Cessnock City Council, part of the Lake Macquarie City Council, part of the Maitland City Council, part of the Newcastle City Council and part of the Port Stephens Council.

Name: Riverina
NameDerivation: Named after the area covered by the electoral division.
LocationDescription: The Division of Riverina consists of Coolamon Shire Council, Cootamundra-Gundagai Regional Council, Cowra Shire Council, Hilltops Council, Junee Shire Council, Lockhart Shire Council, Snowy Valleys Council, Temora Shire Council, Upper Lachlan Shire Council, Wagga Wagga City Council, Weddin Shire Council and Yass Valley Council.

Name: Watson
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Hon. John Christian Watson, 1867-1941. Watson was Prime Minister of Australia (27 April-17 August 1904) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-10).
LocationDescription: The Division of Watson consists of part of the Canterbury Bankstown Council and part of the Strathfield Municipal Council.

Name: Dickson
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir James Robert Dickson, 1832-1901, a leading advocate for Federation, Premier of Queensland (1898-99) and Minister for Defence in the first Federal Ministry.
LocationDescription: The Division of Dickson consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Moreton Bay Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Farming, retail and industrial activities.

Name: Longman
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Irene Maud Longman, 1877-1964, the first woman elected to the Queensland Parliament (1929-32) and at the time only the third woman elected to any Parliament in Australia.  Mrs Longman was actively in involved in issues relating to the family, women and mental health.
LocationDescription: The Division of Longman consists of part of the Moreton Bay Regional Council, part of the Somerset Regional Council and part of the Sunshine Coast Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Tourism, light industry, beef cattle, horse studs, prawn farming, poultry farms, pig farming, and various crops including grains, pineapples, fruit and flower farms.

Name: Blair
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Harold Blair AM, 1924-76, the noted tenor, in recognition of his work for Aboriginal advancement and service to the arts.
LocationDescription: The Division of Blair consists of part of the Brisbane City Council, part of the Ipswich City Council, part of the Scenic Rim Regional Council and part of the Somerset Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Dairy and beef cattle farming, small crop production, commercial, construction and infrastructure industries, tourism and defence.

Name: Lingiari
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Vincent Lingiari AM, 19??-88, who was a member of the Gurindji people from the Victoria River District.  Mr Lingiari was a stockman and land rights leader who worked for many years to improve conditions for Aboriginal people.
LocationDescription: Lingiari covers the majority of the Northern Territory, with the exception of the Darwin Municipality and most of the Palmerston Municipality. Lingiari includes the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands and the Territory of Christmas Island.
ProductsIndustries: Cattle, tourism, horticulture, fishing, light industry in Alice Springs, bauxite, copper, gold and uranium mining.

Name: Solomon
NameDerivation: Named after Vaiben Louis Solomon, 1853-1908. Solomon was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia and a Member of the House of Representatives as the member for the South Australian seat that included the Northern Territory.
LocationDescription: Solomon covers the Darwin Municipality, the  Palmerston Municipality (with the exception of the suburbs of Farrar, Johnston, Mitchell, Yarrawonga and Zuccoli), and the unincorporated areas of the Darwin Rates Act Area and East Arm.
ProductsIndustries: Tourism, mining, horticulture, fishing and light industry.

Name: Bonner
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Neville Thomas Bonner AO, 1922-99, an elder of the Jagera people, in recognition of his service as a Senator for Queensland (1971-83) and leader of indigenous Australia.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bonner consists of part of the Brisbane City Council and part of the Redland City Council.
ProductsIndustries: Industries include tourism, transport, manufacturing and retail. The Port of Brisbane is located in Bonner as are light industrial areas in Murarrie, Hemmant and Lytton.

Name: Flynn
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Reverend John Flynn OBE, 1880-1951, founder of the Royal Flying Doctor Service, who, in the early days of flying and also of radio harnessed both to the relief of suffering and the saving of lives in the remote regions of Queensland and, ultimately, Australia.
LocationDescription: The Division of Flynn consists of Banana Shire Council, Central Highlands Regional Council, Gladstone Regional Council, North Burnett Regional Council, Woorabinda Aboriginal Shire Council, part of the Bundaberg Regional Council, part of the Rockhampton Regional Council and part of the South Burnett Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Primary production including coal, oil, gas, orchards, cotton, grain and cattle. The Port of Gladstone is a major export facility for the area.

Name: McMahon
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir William McMahon GCMG CH, 1908-88. McMahon was Prime Minister of Australia (1971-72) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1949-82).
LocationDescription: The Division of McMahon consists of part of the Blacktown City Council, part of the Cumberland Council, part of the Fairfield City Council and part of the Penrith City Council.

Name: Wright
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Judith Wright, 1915-2000, in recognition of her service and contributions to Australia as a poet, author and social and environmental activist.  Ms Wright was founding president of the Wildlife Preservation Society and a founding member of the Aboriginal Treaty Committee.
LocationDescription: The Division of Wright consists of Lockyer Valley Regional Council, part of the Gold Coast City Council, part of the Ipswich City Council, part of the Logan City Council, part of the Scenic Rim Regional Council and part of the Southern Downs Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Boutique tourism and a wide range of primary production activities.

Name: Bean
NameDerivation: Named after Charles Edwin Woodrow Bean, 1879-1968, Australia's official correspondent to the Australian Imperial Force in World War One, editor of the Official History of Australia in the War of 1914-1918 and primary advocate to establish the Australian War Memorial.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bean covers an area in the south of the ACT consisting of the Districts of Booth, Coree, Cotter River, Mount Clear, Paddys River, Rendezvous Creek, Stromlo, Tennent, Tuggeranong, part of Jerrabomberra, part of Molonglo Valley, part of Weston Creek and part of Woden Valley. The Division of Bean also includes Norfolk Island.
ProductsIndustries: Mainly residential with tourism, retail and some light industry at Hume

Name: Clark
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Andrew Inglis Clark, 1848-1907, in recognition of his contributions to the political and legal systems which have had a lasting and perpetual impact on Australia through his involvement with Federation and the development of the Australian Constitution.
LocationDescription: The Division of Clark is centred on Hobart and consists of the, City of Glenorchy, City of Hobart and part of the Municipality of Kingborough.
ProductsIndustries: Banking and retail, chocolate and confectionery, catamaran construction, brewery, zinc works, food and timber processing, heavy transport, wholesale trade, engineering works, glass products and port facilities at Hobart.

Name: Spence
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Catherine Helen Spence, 1825-1910.  Spence was an advocate for female suffrage and electoral reform and was the first female political candidate in Australia when she stood (unnsuccessfully) for a seat at the Federal Convention election of 1897.
LocationDescription: The Division of Spence consists of City of Playford, Town of Gawler, part of the Barossa Council, part of the City of Salisbury and part of the Light Regional Council.
ProductsIndustries: Commercial, defence, Edinburgh RAAF Base, retail and technology based industry, Lyell McEwin Hospital, market gardens and viticulture.

Name: Brand
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir David Brand KCMG, 1912-79. Brand was Premier of Western Australia (1959-71).
LocationDescription: The Division of Brand consists of the City of Kwinana and part of the City of Rockingham.

Name: Canning
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of Sadie Miriam Canning MBE, 1930-2008, WA's first Indigenous Australian nurse and matron who contributed to health and Indigenous outcomes; and Alfred Wernam Canning, 1860-1936, who surveyed routes for the rabbit-proof fence and cattle stockroutes to the WA goldfields.
LocationDescription: The Division of Canning consists of the City of Mandurah, the Shire of Murray, the Shire of Waroona, part of the City of Rockingham and part of the Shire of Serpentine-Jarrahdale.

Name: Cowan
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Edith Dircksey Cowan OBE, 1861-1932. Cowan was the first woman elected to any Parliament in Australia, state or Commonwealth, when she was elected in 1921 as the Member for West Perth in the Western Australian Legislative Assembly.
LocationDescription: The Division of Cowan consists of part of the City of Joondalup, part of the City of Stirling, part of the City of Swan and part of the City of Wanneroo.

Name: Curtin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of John Joseph Ambrose Curtin, 1885-1945. Curtin was Prime Minister of Australia (1941-45) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1928-31 and 1934-45).
LocationDescription: The Division of Curtin consists of the City of Nedlands, the City of Subiaco, the Shire of Peppermint Grove, the Town of Cambridge, the Town of Claremont, the Town of Cottesloe, the Town of Mosman Park, part of the City of Perth, part of the City of Stirling and part of the City of Vincent.

Name: Forrest
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir John Forrest, 1847-1918. Forrest was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-18).
LocationDescription: The Division of Forrest consists of the City of Bunbury, the City of Busselton, the Shire of Augusta Margaret River, the Shire of Capel, the Shire of Dardanup and the Shire of Harvey.

Name: Fremantle
NameDerivation: Named after the City of Fremantle. The city was named after Captain Charles Howe Fremantle who arrived at the Swan River Colony on 2 May 1829, hoisted the British flag on the South Head, and took formal possession in the name of His Majesty King George IV.
LocationDescription: The Division of Fremantle consists of the City of Fremantle, the Town of East Fremantle, part of the City of Cockburn and part of the City of Melville.

Name: Moore
NameDerivation: Named in honour of George Fletcher Moore, 1798-1886. Throughout the 1830s Moore explored a number of areas in Western Australia and was appointed Advocate-General of the Colony of Western Australia in 1834.
LocationDescription: The Division of Moore consists of part of the City of Joondalup, part of the City of Stirling and part of the City of Wanneroo.

Name: O'Connor
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Charles Yelverton O'Connor, 1843-1902. In 1891, O'Connor became Western Australia's engineer-in-chief and was responsible for designing Fremantle Harbour and the pipeline which supplies Kalgoorlie and other goldfields with water.
LocationDescription: The Division of O'Connor consists of the City of Albany and the Shires of Boddington, Boyup Brook, Bridgetown-Greenbushes, Brookton, Broomehill-Tambellup, Bruce Rock, Collie, Coolgardie, Corrigin, Cranbrook, Cuballing, Denmark, Donnybrook-Balingup, Dumbleyung, Dundas, Esperance, Gnowangerup, Jerramungup, Kalgoorlie-Boulder, Katanning, Kent, Kojonup, Kondinin, Kulin, Lake Grace, Laverton, Leonora, Manjimup, Menzies, Nannup, Narembeen, Narrogin, Ngaanyatjarraku, Pingelly, Plantagenet, Quairading, Ravensthorpe, Wagin, Wandering, West Arthur, Wickepin, Williams, Wiluna, Woodanilling, and Yilgarn.

Name: Pearce
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir George Foster Pearce, 1870-1952. Pearce was a Senator for Western Australia (1901-38) and served as Acting Prime Minister for seven months in 1916.
LocationDescription: The Division of Pearce consists of part of the City of Joondalup, part of the City of Swan and part of the City of Wanneroo.

Name: Perth
NameDerivation: Named after the City of Perth. Under instructions from the Secretary for the Colonies, Sir George Murray, the new town and future seat of government in the Colony of Western Australia was called Perth. Murray was a Perthshire man and represented his birthplace in the House of Commons.
LocationDescription: The Division of Perth consists of the City of Vincent, part of the City of Bayswater, part of the City of Perth and part of the City of Swan.

Name: Swan
NameDerivation: Named after the Swan River. The river was named in 1697 by the Dutch explorer Willem de Vlamingh after the famous black swans of the area.
LocationDescription: The Division of Swan consists of the City of Belmont, the City of South Perth, the Town of Victoria Park, part of the City of Canning, part of the City of Gosnells, part of the City of Kalamunda and part of the City of Swan.

Name: Tangney
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dame Dorothy Margaret Tangney DBE, 1907-85. As a Senator for Western Australia (1943-68), Tangney was the first woman elected to the Senate.
LocationDescription: The Division of Tangney consists of part of the City of Canning, part of the City of Cockburn, part of the City of Gosnells and part of the City of Melville.

Name: Hasluck
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of the Rt Hon Sir Paul Meernaa Caedwalla Hasluck KG GCMG GCVO, 1905-93, Member of the House of Representatives (1949-69) and Governor-General of Australia (1969-74); and Dame Alexandra Margaret Martin Hasluck AD, 1908-93, a noted author.
LocationDescription: The Division of Hasluck consists of the Town of Bassendean, part of the City of Bayswater, part of the City of Belmont, part of the City of Swan and part of the Shire of Mundaring.

Name: Durack
NameDerivation: Named to honour succeeding generations of the Durack family who were pioneers and developers of the Kimberley region.
LocationDescription: The Division of Durack consists of the Cities of Greater Geraldton and Karratha; the Shires of Ashburton, Broome, Carnamah, Carnarvon, Chapman Valley, Chittering, Coorow, Cue, Cunderdin, Dalwallinu, Dandaragan, Derby-West Kimberley, Dowerin, East Pilbara, Exmouth, Gingin, Goomalling, Halls Creek, Irwin, Kellerberrin, Koorda, Meekatharra, Merredin, Mingenew, Moora, Morawa, Mount Magnet, Mount Marshall, Mukinbudin, Murchison, Northampton, Nungarin, Perenjori, Sandstone, Shark Bay, Tammin, Three Springs, Trayning, Upper Gascoyne, Victoria Plains, Westonia, Wongan-Ballidu, Wyalkatchem, Wyndham-East Kimberley, and Yalgoo; the Town of Port Hedland; and part of the City of Swan.

Name: Burt
NameDerivation: Named to honour succeeding generations of the Burt family for their significant contributions to the justice system and public service, specifically Sir Archibald Paull Burt KT, 1810-79; Septimus Burt, 1847-1919; and the Hon Sir Francis Theodore Page Burt AC KCMG QC, 1918-2004.
LocationDescription: The Division of Burt consists of part of the City of Armadale, part of the City of Canning, part of the City of Gosnells and part of the Shire of Serpentine-Jarrahdale.

Name: Aston
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Matilda 'Tilly' Ann Aston, 1873-1947.  Aston was a blind writer and teacher who founded the Victorian Association of Braille Writers in 1894 and the Association for the Advancement of the Blind.  Aston was also the head of the School for the Blind.
LocationDescription: The Division of Aston will consist of Knox City Council and part of the Maroondah City Council.

Name: Ballarat
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division. The name of the city is believed to be derived from the Aboriginal word 'balaarat' meaning resting place or reclining on elbow.
LocationDescription: The Division of Ballarat consists of Ballarat City Council, Hepburn Shire Council, part of the Golden Plains Shire Council, and part of the Moorabool Shire Council.

Name: Bendigo
NameDerivation: Named after the city covered by the electoral division.  The city is named after a Ravenswood shepherd who was nicknamed 'Bendigo' after an English pugilist, Abednego William Thompson.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bendigo consists of Greater Bendigo City Council, Mount Alexander Shire Council, part of the Campaspe Shire Council, part of the Macedon Ranges Shire Council and part of the Mitchell Shire Council.

Name: Bruce
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Lord Stanley Melbourne Bruce CH MC, 1883-1967.  Bruce was Prime Minister of Australia (1923-29) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1918-29 and 1931-33).
LocationDescription: The Division of Bruce consists of part of the Cardinia Shire Council, part of the Casey City Council, part of the Greater Dandenong City Council, and part of the Monash City Council.

Name: Calwell
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Arthur Augustus Calwell, 1896-1973.  Calwell was a Member of the House of Representatives (1940-72).
LocationDescription: The Division of Calwell consists of part of the Hume City Council.

Name: Casey
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Lord Richard Gavin Gardiner Casey KG GCMG CH DSO MC PC, 1890-1976.  Casey was a Member of the House of Representatives (1931-40 and 1949-60) and Governor-General of Australia (1965-69).
LocationDescription: The Division of Casey consists of part of the Cardinia Shire Council, part of the Manningham City Council, part of the Nillumbik Shire Council, and part of the Yarra Ranges Shire Council.

Name: Chisholm
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Caroline Chisholm, 1808-77.  Chisholm was known for her work in encouraging emigration to Australia, her social work in New South Wales and Victoria, particularly with immigrant girls, and the building of shelter sheds along routes to the diggings in the Victorian goldfields.
LocationDescription: The Division of Chisholm consists of part of the Boroondara City Council, part of the Monash City Council, part of the Stonnington City Council, and part of  the Whitehorse City Council.

Name: Corio
NameDerivation: Named after the geographic area covered by the electoral division.  'Corio' is believed to have originated from an Aboriginal word 'coraiyo' meaning small marsupial or sandy cliffs or from the Aboriginal word 'Korayn' meaning salt.
LocationDescription: The Division of Corio consists of part of the Golden Plains Shire Council, part of the Greater Geelong City Council, and part of the Wyndham City Council.

Name: Deakin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Hon. Alfred Deakin, 1856-1919. Deakin was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions that led to the Commonwealth of Australia, Prime Minister of Australia (1903-04, 1905-08 and 1909-10) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1901-13).
LocationDescription: The Division of Deakin consists of part of the Manningham City Council, part of the Maroondah City Council and part of the Whitehorse City Council.

Name: Dunkley
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Louisa Margaret Dunkley, 1866-1927. Dunkley was a union leader and feminist who founded the Victorian Women's Post and Telegraph Association in 1900 and campaigned for equal pay for women.
LocationDescription: The Division of Dunkley consists of Frankston City Council, part of the Kingston City Council, and part of the Mornington Peninsula Shire Council.

Name: Flinders
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Matthew Flinders, 1774-1814. Flinders was a well-known navigator and explorer who charted parts of the Australian coast. The adoption of the name Australia is due to him.
LocationDescription: The Division of Flinders consists of part of the Mornington Peninsula Shire Council and the unincorporated area of French-Elizabeth-Sandstone Islands.

Name: Gellibrand
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Joseph Gellibrand, 1786-1836.  Gellibrand was a lawyer and explorer.
LocationDescription: The Division of Gellibrand consists of part of the Hobsons Bay City Council, and part of Wyndham City Council.

Name: Gippsland
NameDerivation: Named after the geographic area covered by the electoral division.  The south-east region of Victoria was named in March 1840 to honour Sir George Gipps who was Governor of New South Wales at the time.
LocationDescription: The Division of Gippsland consists of East Gippsland Shire Council, Wellington Shire Council, part of Baw Baw Shire Council, part of the Latrobe City Council and the unincorporated area of Gabo Island.

Name: Goldstein
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Vida Jane Goldstein, 1869-1949. Goldstein was a suffragist, feminist and involved in social welfare.  As a Senate candidate in 1903, Goldstein was one of the first women in the British Empire to be nominated for and to stand for election to a national parliament.
LocationDescription: The Division of Goldstein consists of Bayside City Council, part of the Glen Eira City Council, and part of the Kingston City Council.

Name: Holt
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Harold Edward Holt CH, 1908-67.  Holt was Prime Minister of Australia (1966-67) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1935-67).
LocationDescription: The Division of Holt consists of part of the Casey City Council.

Name: Hotham
NameDerivation: Named after Sir Charles Hotham RN KCB, 1806-55.  Hotham was Lieutenant-Governor of Victoria (1854-55) and the first Governor of Victoria (1855).
LocationDescription: The Division of Hotham consists of part of the Glen Eira City Council, part of the Greater Dandenong City Council, part of the Kingston City Council and part of the Monash City Council.

Name: Indi
NameDerivation: Named after an Aboriginal name for the Murray River
LocationDescription: The Division of Indi consists of Alpine Shire Council, Benalla Rural City Council, Indigo Shire Council, Mansfield Shire Council, Murrindindi Shire Council, Towong Shire Council, Wangaratta Rural City Council, Wodonga City Council, part of the Strathbogie Shire Council, part of the Yarra Ranges Shire Council, and the unincorporated areas of Falls Creek Alpine Resort, Lake Mountain Alpine Resort, Mount Buller Alpine Resort, Mount Hotham Alpine Resort, and Mount Stirling Alpine Resort.

Name: Isaacs
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir Isaac Alfred Isaacs GCB GCMG KCMG PC QC, 1855-1948. Isaacs was an active member of the Constitutional Conventions, Member of the House of Representatives (1901-06), Chief Justice of the High Court (1930-31) and the first Australian Governor-General of Australia (1931-36).
LocationDescription: The Division of Isaacs consists of part of the Greater Dandenong City Council and part of the Kingston City Council.

Name: Jagajaga
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the three principal Aboriginal elders who signed a treaty with John Batman in 1835 which intended to give the white settlers 500,000 acres of land at the north-west end of Port Phillip Bay and 100,000 acres around Geelong.
LocationDescription: The Division of Jagajaga consists of Banyule City Council, part of the Manningham City Council, part of the Nillumbik Shire Council, and part of the Whittlesea City Council.

Name: Kooyong
NameDerivation: Named after the geographic location covered at one time by the electoral division. 'Kooyong' is believed to be an Aboriginal word for camp or resting place or possibly derived from the word 'guyun' meaning fighting spear.
LocationDescription: The Division of Kooyong consists of part of the Boroondara City Council, part of the Stonnington City Council, and part of the Yarra City Council.

Name: Lalor
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Peter Lalor, 1827-89. Lalor was leader of the Eureka Stockade rebellion in Ballarat in 1854. In 1855 he was one of the first representatives from the goldfields elected to the Victorian Legislative Council.
LocationDescription: The Division of Lalor consists of part of the Wyndham City Council.

Name: La Trobe
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Charles Joseph La Trobe, 1801-75. La Trobe was the first Lieutenant-Governor of the Colony of Victoria (1851-54).
LocationDescription: The Division of La Trobe consists of part of the Cardinia Shire Council, part of the Casey City Council and part of the Yarra Ranges Shire Council.

Name: Mallee
NameDerivation: Named after the geographic location covered by the electoral division. 'Mallee' is believed to be an Aboriginal word for dwarf eucalypts which grow in the area.
LocationDescription: The Division of Mallee consists of Buloke Shire Council, Central Goldfields Shire Council, Gannawarra Shire Council, Hindmarsh Shire Council, Horsham Rural City Council, Loddon Shire Council, Mildura Rural City Council, Swan Hill Rural City Council, West Wimmera Shire Council, Yarriambiack Shire Council, part of the Northern Grampians Shire Council and part of the Pyrenees Shire Council.

Name: Maribyrnong
NameDerivation: Named after the Maribyrnong River, which is believed to be from: an Aboriginal word for 'yam' or 'edible root', or derived from the Woiwaurrung word 'Mirrangbamurn', with 'mirrang' meaning eye and 'barmurn' ringtail possum, or from the name 'Mareingalk', country belonging to the Mareinbulluc.
LocationDescription: The Division of Maribyrnong consists of part of the Brimbank City Council, part of the Hume City Council,  part of the Melbourne City Council, part of the Merri-bek City Council and part of the Mooonee Valley City Council.

Name: McEwen
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir John McEwen GCMG CH, 1900-80.  McEwen was Prime Minister of Australia (1967-68) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1934-71).
LocationDescription: The Division of McEwen consists of part of the Hume City Council, part of the Macedon Ranges Shire Council, part of the Mitchell Shire Council, part of the Nillumbik Shire Council and part of the Whittlesea City Council.

Name: Melbourne
NameDerivation: Named after the City of Melbourne.  The settlement of Port Phillip was named 'Melbourne' on 5 March 1837 in honour of Lord Melbourne who was the Prime Minister of Great Britain at the time.
LocationDescription: The Division of Melbourne consists of part of the Melbourne City Council, part of the Merri-bek City Council, part of the Moonee Valley City Council, part of the Stonnington City Council and part of the Yarra City Council.

Name: Menzies
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir Robert Gordon Menzies KT CH QC, 1894-1978.  Menzies was Prime Minister of Australia (1939-41 and 1949-66) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1934-66).
LocationDescription: The Division of Menzies consists of part of the Boroondara City Council, part of the Manningham City Council, and part of the Whitehorse City Council.

Name: Scullin
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. James Henry Scullin, 1876-1953.  Scullin was Prime Minister of Australia (1929-32) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1910-13 and 1922-49).
LocationDescription: The Division of Scullin consists of part of the Hume City Council, and part of the Whittlesea City Council.

Name: Wannon
NameDerivation: Named after the Wannon River.  The name 'Wannon' is believed to have been obtained by Major Mitchell from the local Jardwadjali people.
LocationDescription: The Division of Wannon consists of Ararat Rural City Council, Colac Otway Shire Council, Corangamite Shire Council, Glenelg Shire Council, Moyne Shire Council, Southern Grampians Shire Council, Warrnambool City Council, part of the Golden Plains Shire Council, part of the Northern Grampians Shire Council, part of the Pyrenees Shire Council, and part of the Surf Coast Shire Council.

Name: Wills
NameDerivation: Named in honour of William John Wills, 1834-61.  Wills was the surveyor and astronomer of an ultimately unsuccessful 1860 government expedition  to cross Australia from Melbourne to the Gulf of Carpentaria.
LocationDescription: The Division of Wills consists of part of the Melbourne City Council, part of the Merri-bek City Council, part of the Moonee Valley City Council, and part of the Yarra City Council.

Name: Gorton
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. Sir John Grey Gorton GCMG AC CH, 1911-2002.  Gorton was Prime Minister of Australia (1968-71), a Senator for Victoria (1949-68) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1968-75).
LocationDescription: The Division of Gorton consists of part of the Brimbank City Council, and part of the Melton City Council.

Name: Cooper
NameDerivation: Named in honour of William Cooper, 1861-1941. Cooper was a Yorta Yorta man who, as a spokesman for Aboriginal people, called for direct representation in parliament, enfranchisement, land rights and federal control of Aboriginal affairs.
LocationDescription: The Division of Cooper consists of Darebin City Council, part of the Merri-bek City Council, and part of the Yarra City Council.

Name: Fraser
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Rt Hon. John Malcom Fraser AC CH, 1930-2015.  Fraser was Prime Minister of Australia (1975-83) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1955-83).
LocationDescription: The Division of Fraser consists of Maribyrnong City Council, part of the Brimbank City Council, and part of the Hobsons Bay City Council.

Name: Macnamara
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Dame Annie Jean Macnamara DBE, 1899-1968. Macnamara was a medical researcher and doctor who discovered there was more than one type of the polio virus and worked extensively with children suffering from poliomyelitis, training doctors in the management of the disease.
LocationDescription: The Division of Macnamara consists of Port Phillip City Council, part of Glen Eira City Council, part of Melbourne City Council, and part of the Stonnington City Council.

Name: Monash
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Sir John Monash CB(M) KCB(M) GCMG, 1865-1931. Monash was one of the foremost Allied military commanders of the First World War and was recognised for his outstanding contributions to the community.
LocationDescription: The Division of Monash consists of Bass Coast Shire Council, South Gippsland Shire Council, part of the Baw Baw Shire Council, part of the Cardinia Shire Council, part of the Latrobe City Council, part of the Yarra Ranges Shire Council, and the unincorporated area of Mount Baw Baw Alpine Resort.

Name: Nicholls
NameDerivation: Jointly named in honour of Sir Douglas Ralph Nicholls MBE(C) OBE(C) KCVO, 1906-88, a Yorta Yorta, Baraparapa, Dja Dja Wurrung, Jupagalk and Wergaia man, and Lady Gladys Nicholls, 1906-81, a Baraparapa and Dja Dja Wurrung woman, for their roles in advocating for Aboriginal rights and welfare.
LocationDescription: The Division of Nicholls consists of Greater Shepparton City Council, Moira Shire Council, part of the Campaspe Shire Council, part of the Mitchell Shire Council and part of the Strathbogie Shire Council.

Name: Hawke
NameDerivation: Named in honour of the Hon. Robert James Lee Hawke AC, 1929-2019. Hawke was Prime Minister of Australia (1983-91) and a Member of the House of Representatives (1980-92).
LocationDescription: The Division of Hawke consists of part of the Brimbank City Council, part of the Hume City Council, part of the Melton City Council, part of the Moorabool Shire Council, and part of the Wyndham City Council.

Name: Corangamite
NameDerivation: Named after the geographic area covered at one time by the electoral division. 'Corangamite' is believed to be derived from the Gulidjan word for 'bitter water'.
LocationDescription: The Division of Corangamite consists of the Borough of Queenscliffe Council, part of the Greater Geelong City Council, and part of the Surf Coast Shire Council.

Name: Bullwinkel
NameDerivation: Named in honour of Lt Col Vivian Statham (nee Bullwinkel) AO MBE ARRC ED FNM FRCNA, 1915-2000. Bullwinkel was a civilian and military nurse who was the sole survivor of the 1942 Bangka Island massacre and a prisoner of war. The name also honours military medical personnel and prisoners of war.
LocationDescription: The Division of Bullwinkel consists of the Shire of Beverley, the Shire of Northam, the Shire of Toodyay, the Shire of York, part of the City of Armadale, part of the City of Gosnells, part of the City of Kalamunda, part of the City of Swan and part of the Shire of Mundaring.
